version.changelog:
ChainAware Behavioral Prediction MCP v1.0.6

- Removed the skill-card.md file from the repository.
- No other changes to code or functionality.

llm.summary: This skill is a coherent remote ChainAware MCP integration for blockchain wallet and contract risk analysis, with one privacy-documentation gap users should notice.

dimensions.detail: Use of CHAINAWARE_API_KEY, remote network calls, wallet/contract identifiers, and optional x402 payment handling is expected for this service, but users should understand that submitted addresses and operational parameters leave their environment.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a single markdown skill with no executable files or local package install; setup points clients to a remote SSE MCP endpoint.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions are mostly scoped to user-provided wallet, contract, token, network, batch-job, and agent-trust inputs; the privacy section is narrower than the documented tool schemas because some calls also send batch address lists, contract_address, job_id, signature, category, limit, offset, and similar operational fields.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill does not add local persistence or privilege escalation; batch workflows require retaining job_id and signature for follow-up result retrieval, but the artifact does not instruct writing them to disk.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented capabilities match the stated purpose: wallet fraud checks, behavioral profiles, rug-pull prediction, credit scoring, token ranking, batch screening, and related on-chain trust analysis.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, treat ChainAware as an external analytics service: wallet lists, contract addresses, job handles, and some query parameters may be sent to its MCP endpoint. Use a restricted API key where possible, avoid placing keys in connector URLs unless required by the client, and consider whether wallet addresses you process are linked to real users in your regulatory context.
llm.findings: [SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted as a documentation gap: the Data & Privacy section says every tool call sends only walletAddress, network, and apiKey, while the tool docs list additional fields for batch jobs, token ranking, job retrieval, and contract lookups. This is not enough to make the skill suspicious because those fields are purpose-aligned and disclosed elsewhere in the artifact.
